about: Stack budgets read by src/iot/tools/stack_budget.py (ESPR-4). A ratchet: each number is what the code used when it was set, lowered as the code shrinks and raised only in the commit that needs it, with the reason. `goal` is where the 2026-11-13 analysis says the bridge should be on its 4 KB cont stack (an interrupt adds >= 256 B at peak); the gate runs loop() on an 8 KB task stack. The path budget carries 48 B over the measured path for toolchain variance between hosts; frames carry none. The ESP32's GCC 8 cannot write a call graph, so the gate has no path budget.

court_bridge.lowered: Bridge 3.1.0 moved the lifeline (persistence, the portal, the supervisor) out of loop()'s own frame into functions called from its top, and the heartbeat and reply buffers into one static: loop()'s frame went 928 -> 208 B and the deepest path 3,136 -> 2,608 B, so both budgets were lowered with it.
court_bridge.raised: fix/bridge-flows (BR-14): a scan outcome now paints its designed 4-row screen, so applyOutcome calls paintOutcome (a ScreenFacts and a Screen, 176 B) where it called paintLines; the deepest path (scan -> settle -> paint -> MegaTx v2 screen) went 2,608 -> 2,720 B. Still 280 B inside the 3,000 B goal; the new press answers (FSF-11, BR-09) are kept out of handleButton's frame with noinline.

door_gate.raised: Gate 2.0.0's network adoption (devnet::adoptNet: a staged NetSet and the base URL decoded with headroom) is an 832 B frame. The integration first took the 2.0.0 gate from 3,904 B down to this by moving every whole-image temporary off the stack; the gate's loop task is 8 KB and its worst path, measured with the analysis's call-graph tool, was 4,576 B of the 6,000 B the contract allows (device-api.md section 13), measured while that path still ran through the OTA signature check; OTA has since been removed, so the worst path is no deeper than that.
